evidence.field: 字形演變; specimen label and explanatory note
evidence.text: The page labels a sequence of oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, small-seal, and Shuowen forms. It identifies a bronze example as 集成02837 and says the ancient graph depicts clothing with overlapping front lapels. Its accessible text does not date the individual forms or describe a stroke-by-stroke transition.
evidence.title: 漢字「衣」：字形演變

evidence.source: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Multi-function Chinese Character Database
evidence.field: 甲骨部件分析; form, inscriptional uses, Shuowen quotation
evidence.text: The database analyzes oracle-bone and bronze 衣 as an upper garment, with collar, sleeves, and overlapping lapels. It reports oracle-bone uses for place, personal, and sacrificial names; it cites 無叀鼎’s “賜汝玄衣” for an upper-garment use in bronze inscriptions. Its claimed readings of 衣 as 卒 in [冬戈]簋 and as 殷 in 天亡簋 are inscription-specific disputed loan/readings, not evidence that the garment word’s basic meaning was “end” or “sacrifice.” It quotes the Shuowen account but does not establish it independently.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：漢字甲骨部件分析—衣

evidence.source: Shuowen Jiezi quotation via CUHK Multi-function Chinese Character Database
evidence.text: The Han-period dictionary glosses 衣 as 依, distinguishes upper 衣 from lower 裳, and describes the form as 覆二人之形. This is Xu Shen’s account, not independent proof of the graph’s origin; the consulted paleographic analyses interpret the early form as a garment.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：漢字甲骨部件分析—衣

evidence.source: Fudan University Center for the Study of Excavated Texts and Paleography
evidence.field: article interpretation of 大豊（禮）簋 / 天亡簋
evidence.text: 裘錫圭’s 2023 article discusses the disputed inscription phrase and advances a reading and interpretation in which the vessel records King Wu’s ceremony to complete the Heaven-sacrifice left unfinished by King Wen. This materially differs from a reading of 衣 as a loan for 殷 and from the National Museum author’s interpretation of 衣祀 as carrying a shrine tablet to sacrifice to King Wen. The phrase does not securely establish a separate etymology for 衣.
evidence.title: 裘錫圭：大豊（禮）簋銘新釋

evidence.text: Tian Shuai’s 2019 abstract interprets 衣祀于王 as King Wu carrying the ancestral shrine tablet on campaign to sacrifice to King Wen. This differs from readings that take 衣 as a phonetic loan for 殷 or read the graph as 卒; the abstract does not settle the disputed graph and segmentation.
evidence.title: 天亡簋铭文释义补苴

evidence.field: 衣 yī/yì entries; cited literary examples
evidence.text: The dictionary lists yī as upper garment and clothing generally, with examples from the Odes; it lists yì as ‘wear/put on’ with examples from the Analects, Mencius and Han Feizi, and ‘cover/wrap’ with examples from the Yi and Guan Zi. It also lists covering, coating, membrane and moss senses. These are lexical attestations and dictionary senses, not a demonstrated chronology or dated chain of semantic extension.
evidence.title: 衣 yī、yì - 汉典

evidence.source: Baxter and Sagart, 2014 reconstruction table (provided local exact rows checked; table URL inaccessible through web tool)
evidence.field: Baxter–Sagart OC and MC entries; local sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv rows for 衣
evidence.text: The supplied local table rows for 衣 record yī ‘clothes’: MC 'j+j, OC *ʔ(r)əj; and yì ‘wear (v.t.)’: MC 'j+jH, OC *ʔ(r)əj-s. These rows agree with the dossier’s cited transcription. This is a check of the local dataset, not independently inspected external evidence; reconstruction supports a possible *-s contrast but does not prove the verb’s chronology or derivation.
evidence.title: Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1 (13 September 2014)

evidence.source: Local Unihan_Readings.txt row for 衣; official Unicode click-through attempted but inaccessible
evidence.field: kMandarin; local sources/unihan/Unihan_Readings.txt exact row 衣
evidence.text: The supplied local exact row records kMandarin yī for 衣. The official Unihan record for U+8863 was attempted but inaccessible through the web tool, so this is local metadata only and not external verification. Current Mandarin does not establish an ancient sound relationship.
evidence.title: Unicode Unihan record for U+8863 (attempted; inaccessible)

evidence.text: The exact Commons page identifies this as a vector depiction of 衣 in Shuowen seal-script style and provides the original file link. The file is a modern vector redraw, not a photograph of an ancient artifact. Commons records CC0 1.0 for the image.

evidence.text: The exact Commons page identifies this as a modern vector rendering of a Western Zhou bronze-script form and names a Xiaoxuetang record (33.E13F; 頌壺, Western Zhou late, 集成9731) as the specific image source. It gives the original image link and says the file is released under CC0 1.0. It is a redraw of a historical form, not an artifact photograph.

evidence.text: The official notice states that glyph images and glyph-attribute information obtained through the query interface are dedicated under CC0 1.0. This does not grant rights to mirror the database or reuse linked dictionary text.

search_audit.query: 衣 oracle bone bronze form evolution Xiaoxuetang 衣 glyph; 衣 Shuowen oracle bone garment earliest attestation inscriptions 無叀鼎; 衣 Baxter Sagart 2014 Old Chinese clothes wear *ʔ(r)əj
search_audit.outcome: Inspected Academia Sinica and CUHK pages; the Baxter–Sagart PDF URL was inaccessible in this invocation. Its supplied exact local rows were checked separately and are identified as local-only.
Inspected the official notice and guide; they explicitly cover glyph images and glyph attributes obtained through query interface under CC0 1.0.

search_audit.query: 衣-seal.svg Wikimedia Commons; site:xiaoxue.iis.sinica.edu.tw/char 衣 甲骨文 8863 小學堂 字形
search_audit.outcome: Verified the seal-file description and rights, then inspected the Commons bronze-file page for its specific Xiaoxuetang source label and CC0. The incidental Xiaoxuetang candidate result was 女, not 衣, and was not used.

search_audit.query: site:unicode.org/cgi-bin/GetUnihanData.pl?codepoint=8863 衣 kMandarin; 衣 oracle bone forms earliest uses place name sacrificial name Chinese paleography
search_audit.outcome: Official Unicode Unihan record was inaccessible. Inspected CUHK’s reported oracle-bone name uses and bronze clothing use, and Han Dian’s lexical examples/senses.

search_audit.query: 衣-bronze.svg and 衣-oracle.svg Wikimedia Commons exact file descriptions
search_audit.outcome: Bronze form page inspected and sourced to a labeled Western Zhou vessel form. Oracle-file page inspected but its generic drawable form lacks a specimen-level date/source in accessible description; not selected.

gaps: The accessible sources do not date individual early 衣 graph specimens precisely. The oracle-bone uses reported by CUHK are primarily place, personal, and sacrificial-name contexts, while the cited 無叀鼎 garment use is not independently assigned an absolute date in the inspected record.

The path from ‘upper garment’ to clothing generally, object-covering, coating, membrane, or moss is not shown through dated stages. Dictionary citations attest examples and senses, not a chronology of their emergence.

The phrase 衣祀于王 on 天亡簋 remains disputed: 殷 loan reading, 卒 reading, and a distinct ritual interpretation are reported. It cannot securely establish an extra meaning or a whole-graph loan history for 衣.

The Baxter–Sagart primary table and official Unicode Unihan entry were inaccessible through this invocation. Local readings are explicitly reported as local rows only; no external click-through verification is claimed.

The proposed Proto-Sino-Tibetan *w(y)a-t ~ wit comparison and Burmese ဝတ် were not independently verified from an accessible primary comparative source. The proposed sound correspondence and semantic history remain unestablished here.
The Commons glyphs are modern vector redrawings of script forms, not ancient artifact photographs. No direct pixel inspection was performed in this research stage.

The chardb.iis.sinica.edu.tw character database’s rights page says its website content, including images, is protected and reproduction requires permission. No bulk reuse permission for recurring database text was verified, so no local extract is recommended; the selected Commons seal and bronze glyph images have separately stated CC0 provenance.

items.caption: A modern vector rendering of the 衣 form labeled from a late Western Zhou bronze vessel; the Commons page identifies the Xiaoxuetang specimen as 頌壺, 集成9731.
items.alt: Modern outlined bronze-script-style form of 衣, with an open garment-like silhouette.
items.selection_reason: Shows a named, traceable bronze-script example within the supported early garment-pictograph account and has specific source labeling and explicit CC0 rights.
items.rights: CC0 1.0; modern vector redraw sourced to Xiaoxuetang query-interface glyph image.

items.period: Shuowen seal-script style; modern redraw, with no artifact-level date claimed
items.caption: A modern vector rendering of 衣 in Shuowen seal-script style, useful for comparison with the earlier bronze-script form.
items.alt: Outlined seal-script form of 衣, more regularized than the labeled bronze-script drawing.
items.selection_reason: Provides a later conventional script style for comparison with the specifically sourced bronze redraw; it is explicitly identified as a redraw, not an artifact image.
items.rights: CC0 1.0; Wikimedia Commons description states dedication for the image.

limitations.text: Both selected items are modern vector drawings of historical script styles, not photographs or rubbings of ancient objects; no visual inspection of pixels was performed in this research stage.
The bronze image has a specific Xiaoxuetang specimen label, but this research did not inspect an independently dated artifact record. Do not generalize its vessel date label to every bronze form.
